title: Kitab al-Qanun fi al-Tibb
shelf_note: Medici Press 1593 Arabic Canon of Avicenna. It belongs in the McGill/Osler medical-history and Toronto collections.
structure_note: The leaf carries two printed numbers: an Arabic-numeral number in the head and a European-numeral '150' at the foot. That fits the OCR's <page-num>150. The pagination double system and section restarts likely account for most of the 89 backsteps and 370 repeats, so this does not look like a splice. The structure count of pages_translated is 0, but the field says 1022. That is an instrument mismatch, not a defect on the page.

book_verdict: A real and important early Arabic printing of the Canon. On this page, though, the OCR invents a right-margin keyword index that is not on the leaf, and it drops words in several places. One drop leads the translation to make the sea dragon the remedy, and a note backs that misreading with false learning.
